mappings.note: How water reaches the top of a tall tree, plus two other uses of transpiration -- xylem transport, C 4.3-LO-1.
Pancreatic juice cannot act in the stomach because its enzymes need an alkaline medium. A condition of human digestion, C 3.2-LO-1, not a C 1.3 acid-base item.
Why the medium shifts from acidic in the stomach to alkaline in the small intestine -- bile and pancreatic juice neutralising chyme. Part of the digestion sequence, C 3.2-LO-1.
The salivary enzyme digesting starch is amylase -- C 3.2-LO-1.
Matching amylase, pepsin, lipase and trypsin to starch, stomach protein, fat and intestinal protein -- enzyme-to-substrate within human digestion, C 3.2-LO-1.
Stomata close when guard cells lose water and go flaccid. The cell-level water mechanism, C 3.1, rather than the gas-exchange process C 3.2.
True/false: stomata usually close at night. Turns on guard-cell turgor, so C 3.1 for consistency with qid:707083.
What life processes are. Names the whole set rather than any one of them, so the competency C 3.2 -- none of LO-1, LO-2 or LO-3 covers the general definition.
Explain life processes and why nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion are each essential. Explicitly spans all four, so the competency C 3.2, matching qid:707085 and qid:85597.
How autotrophic nutrition differs from heterotrophic -- the first clause of C 3.2-LO-1, as for qid:85598.

The events of photosynthesis in sequence and how each raw material reaches the chloroplast. The chloroplast is named but as a destination, not as the object of study, so this stays at C 3.2-LO-1 rather than C 3.1.
What peristaltic movements are -- a step in the human nutrition sequence, C 3.2-LO-1.

Why ATP is the energy currency of the cell. It is the form respiration's released energy is stored in, and 'the energy released' is the clause that distinguishes C 3.2-LO-3. Mapped the same way as qid:104728.
Why arteries are thick and elastic while veins carry valves -- pressure in the two vessel types, C 3.2-LO-2.
True/false: all arteries carry oxygenated blood (false -- the pulmonary artery does not). Vessels of the human transport pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Name the two conducting tissues in plants and what each carries -- xylem and phloem, C 4.3-LO-1.
True/false: phloem transport needs energy while xylem transport does not. A direct xylem/phloem contrast, C 4.3-LO-1.
Three types of heterotrophic nutrition with examples -- saprophytic, parasitic and holozoic. The heterotrophic clause of C 3.2-LO-1.
Describe the human circulatory system, naming its parts and their functions -- C 3.2-LO-2, which asks for the transport pathway and the organs involved.

Matching red blood cell, platelet, capillary and vein valve to their functions -- components of human transport, C 3.2-LO-2. C 4.2-LO-1 was considered for the capillary but that outcome names only the alveolus, nephron and villus.
